title: Lewis Dot Structures of Common Compounds
topicTitle: Lewis dot structure of some common compounds of s and p block elements
notes:
## 1. Topic Introduction — Chemistry in Dots and Lines

A Lewis dot structure is a molecule's electron budget made visible: every valence electron accounted for, either as a bonding pair (a line) or a lone pair (dots). Draw it correctly and the shape, polarity and reactivity of the molecule follow almost mechanically. NEB has asked the CO₂ dot structure directly (2022, 2024) and the H₂O/NH₃ structures with their shapes (2024) — this topic is the drawing manual.

## 2. Fundamental Concepts

### 2.1 The drawing procedure

1. **Count** total valence electrons (adjust for charge: add for anions, subtract for cations).
2. **Choose the skeleton** — least electronegative atom central (H is always terminal).
3. **Place one bond pair** between every connected pair; complete the octets (duets for H) of outer atoms with lone pairs.
4. **Park leftovers on the central atom**; if its octet is short, convert outer lone pairs into double/triple bonds.
5. **Verify:** electrons used = electrons counted; every atom at its octet (or a known exception: Be, B, expanded P/S).

### 2.2 The standard gallery (s and p block)

- **H₂O:** 8 e⁻ → two O–H bonds + **two lone pairs** on O (bent, 104.5°).
- **NH₃:** 8 e⁻ → three N–H bonds + **one lone pair** (pyramidal, 107°).
- **CH₄:** 8 e⁻ → four C–H bonds, no lone pairs (tetrahedral, 109.5°).
- **CO₂:** 16 e⁻ → two C=O double bonds, two lone pairs per O (linear, 180°).
- **BF₃:** 24 e⁻ → three B–F bonds, no lone pair on B — **incomplete octet (6 e⁻)** (trigonal planar, 120°).
- **PCl₅:** 40 e⁻ → five P–Cl bonds — **expanded octet (10 e⁻)** (trigonal bipyramidal).
- **SF₆:** 48 e⁻ → six S–F bonds — **expanded octet (12 e⁻)** (octahedral).
- **H₂S:** 8 e⁻ → two S–H bonds + two lone pairs (bent, 92°).

### 2.3 Formal charge — choosing between rival structures

- **FC = valence e⁻ − (non-bonding e⁻ + ½ bonding e⁻).**
- The best structure minimises formal charges and puts negative FC on the more electronegative atom.
- Example O₃: the two resonance forms each carry FC +1 on central O and −1 on one terminal O — formal charge bookkeeping justifies resonance (topic 31).

### 2.4 Polyatomic ions

- **NH₄⁺:** 5 + 4 − 1 = 8 e⁻ → four N–H bonds; formal charge +1 on N.
- **OH⁻:** 6 + 1 + 1 = 8 e⁻ → one O–H bond, three lone pairs, FC −1 on O.
- **CO₃²⁻:** 4 + 18 + 2 = 24 e⁻ → one C=O, two C–O⁻, one lone pair on C — and resonance spreads the double bond (topic 31).

## 3. Scientific Definitions

| Term | Scientific meaning | Value to quote |
|---|---|---|
| **Lewis structure** | Diagram of valence electrons as dots/lines showing bonding and lone pairs | CO₂: O=C=O |
| **Lone pair** | Valence pair not shared between atoms | H₂O: 2 LP |
| **Bonding pair** | Electron pair shared between two atoms | CH₄: 4 BP |
| **Formal charge** | FC = valence e⁻ − (non-bonding e⁻ + ½ bonding e⁻) | O₃: +1/−1/0 |
| **Expanded octet** | More than 8 e⁻ around central atom (period ≥ 3) | SF₆: 12 e⁻ |

## 4. Detailed Explanation

### 4.1 Verified PYQ (NEB 2022 & 2024): Lewis dot structure of CO₂ and its shape

- Count: 4 + 2(6) = **16 electrons**.
- Skeleton O–C–O; place one pair in each C–O bond (4 e⁻), complete O octets with lone pairs (12 e⁻) — carbon has only 4 e⁻.
- Convert one lone pair from each O into a bonding pair → **O=C=O**, two double bonds.
- Each atom reaches an octet; all 16 electrons placed. **Shape: linear, 180°** (two electron domains around C).

### 4.2 Verified PYQ (NEB 2024): Lewis structures of H₂O and NH₃ with VSEPR shapes

- **H₂O:** 6 + 2(1) = 8 e⁻ → two O–H bonds + two lone pairs on O. Four electron domains → tetrahedral electron geometry, but **molecular shape bent (V-shaped), ≈104.5°** — lone pairs compress the angle.
- **NH₃:** 5 + 3(1) = 8 e⁻ → three N–H bonds + one lone pair. Four domains → **pyramidal shape, ≈107°** — one lone pair compresses 109.5° to 107°.

### 4.3 Reading the exceptions straight off the dots

- BF₃'s drawing forces 6 electrons onto B — the structure itself announces the incomplete octet and the Lewis-acid character.
- PCl₅/SF₆ demand 10/12 electrons on the central atom — only legal for period ≥ 3.
- The dot count is also the raw material for VSEPR: **bonding pairs + lone pairs = electron domains**, and domains set the shape (topic 32).

### Deep dive — a reliable procedure for any Lewis structure

Work the same five steps every time: (1) count **total valence electrons** (add for anions, subtract for cations); (2) pick the least electronegative atom (never H) as central; (3) draw single bonds and complete octets of outer atoms; (4) put leftover electrons on the central atom; (5) if the central atom falls short of an octet, convert lone pairs into double/triple bonds, and check formal charges to pick the best structure.

Formal charge = valence e⁻ − (nonbonding e⁻ + ½ bonding e⁻). The best structure minimises formal charges and puts negative charge on the more electronegative atom — which is why the CO₃²⁻ three-form resonance set and the O₃ structure (central O = +1, terminal O = −1) are the exam standards. Watch the two traps: total electrons ≠ dots on one atom (CO₂ has 16), and BF₃ is *correctly* drawn with 6 electrons on boron — forcing a double bond would put formal charges the wrong way.

**Lewis structures of the standard exam set**

| Species | Total valence e⁻ | Structure (skeleton) | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| H₂O | 8 | H–O–H with 2 lone pairs on O | Bent, 104.5° |
| NH₃ | 8 | N with 3 N–H + 1 lone pair | Pyramidal, 107° |
| CH₄ | 8 | C with 4 C–H bonds | Tetrahedral, 109.5° |
| CO₂ | 16 | O=C=O, two double bonds | Linear, no lone pairs on C |
| CO₃²− | 24 | One C=O + two C–O⁻, resonance over 3 forms | All C–O equal (129 pm) |
| BF₃ | 24 | B with 3 B–F, 6 e⁻ on B | Electron-deficient Lewis acid |

## 5. Comparison Tables

**Molecule-by-molecule dot audit**

| Molecule | Total e⁻ | Bonds | Lone pairs (central) | Shape |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| H₂O | 8 | 2 O–H | 2 | Bent 104.5° |
| NH₃ | 8 | 3 N–H | 1 | Pyramidal 107° |
| CH₄ | 8 | 4 C–H | 0 | Tetrahedral 109.5° |
| CO₂ | 16 | 2 C=O | 0 | Linear 180° |
| BF₃ | 24 | 3 B–F | 0 | Trigonal planar 120° |
| PCl₅ | 40 | 5 P–Cl | 0 | Trigonal bipyramidal |
| SF₆ | 48 | 6 S–F | 0 | Octahedral |
| H₂S | 8 | 2 S–H | 2 | Bent ≈92° |

**Formal charge worked: O₃**

| Atom | valence e⁻ | non-bonding | ½ bonding | FC |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Central O | 6 | 2 | 3 | +1 |
| Double-bond O | 6 | 4 | 2 | 0 |
| Single-bond O | 6 | 6 | 1 | −1 |

## 6. Common Confusions

**Lone pairs are not optional decoration:** omitting them changes the VSEPR count and hence the predicted shape — H₂O without its lone pairs would be drawn "linear" and lose all the marks.
**Total electrons ≠ electrons shown as dots around one atom:** in CO₂ the 16 electrons distribute over three atoms; the audit line "used = counted" is the safety check.
**Formal charge ≠ real charge:** it is a bookkeeping index for choosing among structures; the molecule's real charge distribution comes from electronegativity (partial charges), not FC.

## 7. Exam Application

**Verified PYQ (NEB 2022/2024): Write the Lewis dot structure of CO₂. What is its molecular shape?** — 16 valence electrons; O=C=O with two lone pairs on each oxygen; carbon's octet completed by two double bonds. Two electron domains, no lone pairs on C → **linear, 180°**, and the two C=O bond dipoles cancel, making the molecule non-polar.

**Verified PYQ (NEB 2024): Draw the Lewis structures of H₂O and NH₃ and predict their shapes using VSEPR theory.** — H₂O: two bonds + two lone pairs → bent, ≈104.5°. NH₃: three bonds + one lone pair → pyramidal, ≈107°. Both angles sit below 109.5° because lone pair–bond pair repulsion exceeds bond pair–bond pair repulsion.

**NEB-style (2m): Draw the Lewis structure of BF₃ and comment on boron's octet.** — 24 valence electrons; three B–F single bonds, three lone pairs on each F; boron holds only 6 electrons — an incomplete octet, making BF₃ a strong Lewis acid that completes its octet by accepting a pair (e.g. from NH₃).
confusion: **Draw lone pairs first, shapes later:** every VSEPR answer begins with the completed Lewis structure — lone pairs included — or the domain count collapses.

**Formal charge vs oxidation state:** FC assigns bonding electrons equally; oxidation state assigns them to the more electronegative atom — the two bookkeeping systems give different numbers on purpose.

practiceQuestions: **NEB 2022 & 2024 (2m): Write the Lewis dot structure of CO₂. What is its molecular shape?** — Carbon dioxide has 4 + 2(6) = **16 valence electrons**. Skeleton O–C–O: one pair in each C–O link, six electrons (three lone pairs) on each oxygen complete their octets but leave carbon with only four. Moving one lone pair from each oxygen into bonding gives **O=C=O** — two double bonds, two lone pairs per oxygen, every atom at an octet. Carbon carries two electron domains and no lone pairs, so VSEPR gives a **linear molecule, 180°**; the equal, opposite C=O dipoles cancel and CO₂ is non-polar.

**NEB 2024 (3m): Draw the Lewis structures of H₂O and NH₃ and predict their shapes using VSEPR theory.** — **H₂O:** 8 valence electrons → two O–H bonding pairs plus **two lone pairs** on oxygen. Four electron domains give tetrahedral electron geometry; the two lone pairs push the bonds together, so the molecular shape is **bent (V-shaped) with H–O–H ≈ 104.5°**. **NH₃:** 8 valence electrons → three N–H bonds plus **one lone pair** on nitrogen. Four domains again, but one lone pair compresses the angle less: **pyramidal shape, H–N–H ≈ 107°**. Both angles fall below the ideal 109.5° because lone pair–bond pair repulsion exceeds bond pair–bond pair repulsion.

**NEB-style (2m): Compute the formal charges in the ozone molecule and state what they imply.** — For O₃ (central O double-bonded to one O, single-bonded to the other): central O = 6 − (2 + 3) = **+1**; double-bond terminal O = 6 − (4 + 2) = **0**; single-bond terminal O = 6 − (6 + 1) = **−1**. The mirror-image structure carries the −1 on the other terminal oxygen. Neither structure alone is real — the charges and the two different O–O lengths (128 and 136 pm) show the true molecule is a **resonance hybrid** of the two forms.

- Total valence e⁻ = Σ(valence e⁻) ± charge
- FC = V − (N + ½B)
- Domains = bonding pairs + lone pairs (central atom)

summary: A Lewis structure is an electron audit made visible. Count the valence electrons (adjusting for charge), pick the least electronegative central atom, spend electrons on bonds first and outer octets second, park the remainder on the centre, and promote lone pairs to double or triple bonds when the central octet falls short. The gallery every exam draws from: **H₂O** (2 bonds + 2 lone pairs, bent 104.5°), **NH₃** (3 + 1, pyramidal 107°), **CH₄** (4 + 0, tetrahedral 109.5°), **CO₂** (two C=O, linear 180° — NEB 2022 and 2024), **BF₃** (incomplete octet, 6 e⁻), **PCl₅** (10 e⁻) and **SF₆** (12 e⁻) as expanded-octet legal cases, **H₂S** (bent ≈92°). Formal charge (V − N − ½B) referees rival structures and sets up resonance. Lone pairs are never optional: they are the hinge between the dot picture and the VSEPR shape.

**Verified PYQ (NEB 2024): Draw the Lewis structures of H₂O and NH₃ and predict their shapes using VSEPR theory.** — H₂O: two bonds + two lone pairs → bent, ≈104.5°. NH₃: three bonds + one lone pair → pyramidal, ≈107°. Both angles sit below 109.5° because lone pair–bond pair repulsion exceeds bond pair–bond pair repulsion.

**NEB-style (2m): Draw the Lewis structure of BF₃ and comment on boron's octet.** — 24 valence electrons; three B–F single bonds, three lone pairs on each F; boron holds only 6 electrons — an incomplete octet, making BF₃ a strong Lewis acid that completes its octet by accepting a pair (e.g. from NH₃).
confusion: **Draw lone pairs first, shapes later:** every VSEPR answer begins with the completed Lewis structure — lone pairs included — or the domain count collapses.

**Formal charge vs oxidation state:** FC assigns bonding electrons equally; oxidation state assigns them to the more electronegative atom — the two bookkeeping systems give different numbers on purpose.
keyPoints: Procedure: count valence e⁻ (± charge) → skeleton (least EN central) → bonds → outer octets → leftovers on central atom → double/triple bonds if short → verify. Gallery: H₂O (2 LP, bent), NH₃ (1 LP, pyramidal), CH₄ (tetrahedral), CO₂ (2 C=O, linear), BF₃ (6 e⁻, trigonal planar), PCl₅ (10 e⁻, TBP), SF₆ (12 e⁻, octahedral), H₂S (bent ≈92°). Formal charge = valence − (non-bonding + ½ bonding); minimise FC, negative on the more EN atom.
importantConcepts: The Lewis structure is the input to VSEPR: bonding pairs + lone pairs = electron domains. Lone pairs on the central atom are the difference between electron geometry and molecular shape — omit them and every downstream answer is wrong.
examples: ***CO₂'s 16 electrons: 8 in two double bonds, 8 in four lone pairs*** — the full audit, quoted in NEB 2022 and 2024.
universalFacts: BF₃'s 6-electron boron is the textbook Lewis acid: it completes its octet by accepting NH₃'s lone pair, forming the NH₃·BF₃ adduct.
importantStatements: "A Lewis structure represents valence electrons as dots, with shared pairs drawn as lines, such that each atom attains its octet (or a recognised exception)."
importantNotes: Verified PYQs: NEB 2022 and NEB 2024 — CO₂ dot structure + shape; NEB 2024 — H₂O/NH₃ Lewis structures + VSEPR shapes; all solved above. Other items are NEB-style practice.
examShortTricks: Electron budget quickies: H₂O/NH₃/CH₄ = 8; CO₂ = 16; BF₃ = 24; PCl₅ = 40; SF₆ = 48. "Least EN central, H always terminal."
examNotes: In shape questions, write three lines: Lewis structure → electron domains (bonds + lone pairs) → shape + angle with the lone-pair compression remark. That structure matches the mark scheme.
formulas:
- Total valence e⁻ = Σ(valence e⁻) ± charge
- FC = V − (N + ½B)
- Domains = bonding pairs + lone pairs (central atom)

Why must hydrogen always occupy a terminal position in a Lewis structure?
Draw SO₂ and explain why sulphur carries a lone pair despite two S=O-style links.
practiceQuestions: **NEB 2022 & 2024 (2m): Write the Lewis dot structure of CO₂. What is its molecular shape?** — Carbon dioxide has 4 + 2(6) = **16 valence electrons**. Skeleton O–C–O: one pair in each C–O link, six electrons (three lone pairs) on each oxygen complete their octets but leave carbon with only four. Moving one lone pair from each oxygen into bonding gives **O=C=O** — two double bonds, two lone pairs per oxygen, every atom at an octet. Carbon carries two electron domains and no lone pairs, so VSEPR gives a **linear molecule, 180°**; the equal, opposite C=O dipoles cancel and CO₂ is non-polar.

**NEB 2024 (3m): Draw the Lewis structures of H₂O and NH₃ and predict their shapes using VSEPR theory.** — **H₂O:** 8 valence electrons → two O–H bonding pairs plus **two lone pairs** on oxygen. Four electron domains give tetrahedral electron geometry; the two lone pairs push the bonds together, so the molecular shape is **bent (V-shaped) with H–O–H ≈ 104.5°**. **NH₃:** 8 valence electrons → three N–H bonds plus **one lone pair** on nitrogen. Four domains again, but one lone pair compresses the angle less: **pyramidal shape, H–N–H ≈ 107°**. Both angles fall below the ideal 109.5° because lone pair–bond pair repulsion exceeds bond pair–bond pair repulsion.

**NEB-style (2m): Compute the formal charges in the ozone molecule and state what they imply.** — For O₃ (central O double-bonded to one O, single-bonded to the other): central O = 6 − (2 + 3) = **+1**; double-bond terminal O = 6 − (4 + 2) = **0**; single-bond terminal O = 6 − (6 + 1) = **−1**. The mirror-image structure carries the −1 on the other terminal oxygen. Neither structure alone is real — the charges and the two different O–O lengths (128 and 136 pm) show the true molecule is a **resonance hybrid** of the two forms.

universalFacts: BF₃'s 6-electron boron is the textbook Lewis acid: it completes its octet by accepting NH₃'s lone pair, forming the NH₃·BF₃ adduct.

mindmap.centralConcept: Lewis structures — drawing where the electrons are

subtopics.name: Step-by-step construction
points: Count total valence electrons from all atoms, adjusting for charge
Connect atoms with single bonds, then place remaining electrons as lone pairs
Form multiple bonds if an octet is still incomplete

subtopics.name: Formal charge
points: Formal charge = valence electrons - (lone pair electrons/2) - bonds
The structure with formal charges closest to zero is preferred
Negative formal charge belongs on the more electronegative atom

branches.topic: Level 2 — Core: s and p block examples

subtopics.name: Common structures
points: H2O: two O-H bonds plus two lone pairs on oxygen, bent
NH3: three N-H bonds plus one lone pair, pyramidal
CO2: two double bonds, linear, no lone pairs on carbon

subtopics.name: Expanded octet cases
points: PCl5 has five bonding pairs on phosphorus — 10 electrons
SF6 has six bonding pairs on sulfur — 12 electrons
Only period 3 elements and below can expand their octet

subtopics.name: Resonance structures
points: When more than one valid Lewis structure exists, the real molecule is a hybrid
Ozone and carbonate ion are standard examples
Resonance stabilises the molecule by delocalising electrons

subtopics.name: Limits of the Lewis model
points: Gives no information about bond angles or three-dimensional shape
Molecular orbital theory is required for these
